candidate_relations.reason: Bird exposure and cerebral mass lesions fit cryptococcal disease rather than coccidioidomycosis.
The occipital lesions are infectious cryptococcomas rather than a primary brain tumor.
A subacute mass-lesion presentation with vasogenic edema is not a neurodegenerative disease.
Dementia-like confusion is a manifestation of the cerebral lesions rather than the etiologic diagnosis.
Infection is the correct broad category but omits Cryptococcus and the localized granulomatous brain mass.
The focal occipital mass lesions are incompatible with subacute sclerosing panencephalitis.
No Toxoplasma evidence is provided, and the final lesions are cryptococcal.
Cysticercosis is a distinct parasitic cause of brain lesions from cryptococcoma.
Primary CNS lymphoma is a differential mass lesion but not equivalent to cryptococcoma.
Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy causes white-matter disease rather than resectable edematous cryptococcomas.
No systemic malignancy is present and the lesions are infectious rather than metastatic.
Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease does not present as two focal edematous occipital masses.
Primary CNS lymphoma is not the cryptococcal granulomatous lesion.
Histoplasmosis is a distinct fungal etiology from Cryptococcus.
Although cryptococcoma mimics a brain tumor radiographically, it is an infectious granuloma rather than a neoplasm.
Toxoplasmosis is not supported and is etiologically distinct from cryptococcoma.
Cryptococcosis identifies the causative infection but omits the localized cerebral mass-forming cryptococcoma subtype.
